title: Third-party script loaded with no integrity hash
msg: External script is loaded without an integrity= hash, so the page accepts whatever that host serves today. Req 6.4.3 requires each script to be authorised and its integrity assured.
fix: Add integrity="sha384-..." plus crossorigin="anonymous", or self-host the file.

title: integrity= present but crossorigin= missing
msg: integrity= is set but crossorigin= is not, so the browser fetches the script in no-cors mode and silently skips the hash check. The page looks pinned and is not.
fix: Add crossorigin="anonymous" to the same tag.

title: External stylesheet with no integrity hash
msg: A cross-origin stylesheet is loaded without integrity=. CSS on a payment page can restyle or overlay the card field, so it is in scope for script authorisation.
fix: Add integrity= and crossorigin="anonymous", or self-host the stylesheet.

title: No Content-Security-Policy on the payment page
msg: No Content-Security-Policy is declared or documented in this page. Without one there is no allow-list of script origins and no violation signal to alert on.
fix: Add a <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy"> tag, or document the response header in a comment in this file.

title: CSP allows unsafe-inline, unsafe-eval or a wildcard script source
msg: The Content-Security-Policy contains 'unsafe-inline', 'unsafe-eval' or a wildcard script source, which lets any injected tag run. The policy is present but it authorises nothing.
fix: Replace inline allowances with per-request nonces and list script origins explicitly.

title: Inline script with no nonce
msg: An inline <script> block has no nonce= attribute, so it can only run under a CSP that also permits injected inline scripts.
fix: Add nonce="..." matching the per-response nonce in your CSP.

title: Session-replay or heatmap script on the payment page
msg: A session-replay or heatmap recorder is loaded on the page that handles card entry. These tools capture keystrokes and DOM state, which can send the PAN and the CVV to a third party.
fix: Remove the recorder from payment pages, or scope its snippet to non-payment routes.

title: Tag manager on the payment page
msg: A tag manager or third-party tag container is loaded on the payment page. It can inject arbitrary scripts after deployment, which defeats the script authorisation inventory Req 6.4.3 asks for.
fix: Exclude payment pages from the container, or pin the exact scripts you need directly.

title: Card number field rendered in the merchant page
msg: A card number input lives in your own DOM rather than in a hosted field or iframe from the payment provider. That moves the page from SAQ A into SAQ A-EP and pulls every script on it into scope.
fix: Swap the input for the provider's hosted field or iframe.

title: CVV / security code field in the merchant page
msg: A security code input is rendered in your own DOM. The CVV is sensitive authentication data and must never be storable or readable by page scripts after authorisation.
fix: Use the provider's hosted CVV field.

title: Resource loaded over plain http://
msg: A resource on the payment page is loaded over plain http://. It can be read and rewritten in transit, and the browser may block or downgrade the page.
fix: Load every payment-page resource over https://.

title: Form posts to a plain http:// endpoint
msg: The checkout form posts to a plain http:// endpoint, so the submitted values cross the network unprotected.
fix: Point the form action at an https:// endpoint.

title: Script element built at runtime
msg: The page builds a script element at runtime (document.write or createElement('script')), so the set of scripts that actually run is not visible in this file and cannot be inventoried from source.
fix: Declare the script statically with an integrity hash, or record it in your authorised-script inventory.

title: Card-shaped value written to browser storage
msg: A card-shaped key is written to localStorage or sessionStorage. Cardholder data must not be persisted in the browser, and sensitive authentication data must not be stored after authorisation at all.
fix: Keep the value in memory only, or hold the provider's opaque token instead.

title: No change-and-tamper detection endpoint
msg: The page declares no report-to, report-uri or Reporting-Endpoints target, so a changed HTTP header or script element on the payment page raises no alert. Req 11.6.1 asks for a detection mechanism that alerts personnel.
fix: Add report-to (with a Reporting-Endpoints header) to the CSP and route it to a monitored endpoint.
